learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Electrical Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Basic knowledge and application of environmental technologies and sustainability.
Identify environmental aspects of different industrial activities, selecting the most significant ones.
Identify legal requirements regarding pollution prevention and control.
Apply methods for assessing environmental impacts.
Manage preventive and corrective environmental management instruments: environmental impact assessment, environmental management systems, environmental audits.
Propose methodologies for the treatment, valorization, and disposal of effluents and waste.

syllabus_topics: INTRODUCTION
Topic 1. Introduction to the environment and sustainable development
AIR POLLUTION AND TECHNOLOGIES FOR AIR POLLUTION PREVENTION
Topic 2 General aspects of air pollution
Topic 3. Air pollution measurements
Topic 4. Dispersion of pollutants in the atmosphere
Topic 5. Control technologies for particle removal
Topic 6. Control technologies for gaseous pollutant removal
Topic 7. Sound, noise and acoustic pollution
WATER POLLUTION AND TECHNOLOGIES FOR WATER POLLUTION PREVENTION
Topic 8. General aspects of water pollution
Topic 9. Impacts of pollutants on water. Discharge regulations
Topic 10 Physical treatments for water pollution reduction
Topic 11 Biological treatments for water pollution reduction
Topic 12 Chemical treatments for water pollution reduction
Topic 13 Sludges generated in wastewater treatment
TECHNOLOGIES FOR THE REDUCTION, VALORIZATION AND DISPOSAL OF URBAN AND INDUSTRIAL SOLID WASTE
Topic 14. General aspects of waste pollution
Topic 15. Management, treatment and disposal of domestic waste
Topic 16. Industrial waste. Management, treatment and disposal of hazardous waste
ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT
Topic 17. Environmental prevention: IPPC Directive. Environmental impact assessment
Topic 18. Environmental management instruments: Environmental management systems, Audits and Life Cycle Analysis

assessment_methods.method: Exercises, assignments and presentations developed during the course (classroom practices and group tutorials)

assessment_rules: For ordinary evaluation, the final grade is composed of 65% theoretical/practical exams, 20% course assignments/presentations, and 15% laboratory practices. A minimum of 40% (4/10) in each section (exams, assignments/presentations, laboratory practices) is required to pass the subject. The theoretical/practical exam consists of a theory part and a problem-solving part, each scored out of 5, with a minimum of 1.5 in each required. Laboratory practice work and report also require a minimum of 4/10 each. In extraordinary calls, the exam covers the entire subject, and the same percentages and minimums apply; however, students who did not meet minimum attendance or minimum grades in classroom practices or group tutorials can still be evaluated. A practical exam for laboratory practices is available for students who did not pass them in the first call.
